messages:
maya: seeing weird token delta for a customer using streaming + toolcalls. they say billed tokens > tokens seen in logs. anyone else?
sanjay: saw a report this morning, looks like retries + truncation interaction. can you paste the trace id?
maya: trace=tr-9f2c, sample payload attached (short). user did a streaming request, model made a toolcall that returned a 9k-char blob, client truncated display to 512 chars and re-requested to fetch rest (client retry with same request_id). billing shows both the full tool response and the retry counted.
frank: hmm. are retries using the same idempotency key? our ingest uses request_id header + sequence offsets for stream fragments. if client re-issues a top-level request instead of using stream resume, we might treat it as new and bill again.
lisa: also note truncation path: we have code that marks a toolcall as "complete" once stream EOF seen; if client truncates early we might still have recorded the full tool output length when it was generated by the tool plugin before truncation happened at the client side. billing then charges for generated tokens even though client only read a prefix.
maya: right — customer's complaint: they expected charges only for what was delivered to them, not for the entire tool output that was generated then truncated by UI.
sanjay: billing contract currently: charge for model input + model output + tool outputs generated by tool integrations. we don't have a rule that deducts tokens for unread/truncated bytes. that's intentional historically (we billed for generation). but streaming + retries plus UI truncation creates double-charge when retries re-generate.
frank: short-term fix idea: dedupe billing by request_id + model_name + tool_call_id. If a subsequent retry uses same request_id, ignore tokens already accounted for.
lisa: can we guarantee clients will send same request_id for resume? not all clients do. mobile clients often re-try with new id. we should make server-side resumable fragments keyed by session id + user id + prompt hash perhaps.
maya: another complexity: streaming fragments are billed as they are produced; if a fragment fails mid-stream and is retried, we might bill both fragments. we need idempotent fragment markers from runtime: sequence_no + fragment_id so retries that replay fragments with same fragment_id do not re-bill.
frank: agree. runtime currently emits "fragment_sent(fragment_id, tokens)" events to meter. change: meter should maintain short-lived ledger of fragment_ids for X minutes to dedupe. we already have a cache for ephemeral traces; extend TTL to cover typical client retry windows (30s).
sanjay: here's pseudocode for meter change:
// when fragment event arrives
if (!ledger.contains(fragment_id)) {
  ledger.add(fragment_id, token_count)
  bill(token_count)
} else {
  // duplicate fragment replay, ignore
}
ledger entries expire after 30s

lisa: what about toolcalls where tool generates additional tokens server-side after we already billed the initial streaming chunk? Example: tool streams first chunk, we bill, then tool produces more and we bill again. That's expected if more content actually generated. Issue is when the client truncates view but tool kept producing and we billed for entire tool output even though customer thinks they didn't receive it. Need to clarify billing policy to customers or implement "bill-for-delivered" mode for streaming UIs.
maya: business asked to avoid surprise bills. can we make default UX "bill-for-delivered" for streaming that are proxied through Console/SDKs? That would require meter to only bill tokens that were ACKed by downstream consumer (ack per fragment). For hosted API direct customers we keep bill-for-generated.
frank: feasible: add ack channel between client SDK/console and meter. SDK emits ACK(fragment_id) when UI renders or client chooses to accept. cost: increases client complexity and potential under-billing if ACKs lost. fallback: default to generated billing but provide opt-in "ack-based" billing for customers who want strict delivered semantics.
sanjay: rollout plan: 1) dedupe by fragment_id for 30s (low risk infra change). 2) add request_id-level dedupe for toolcall top-level retry replay. 3) design ack-based delivered-billing as feature (needs product + contract signoff).
lisa: telemetry/dashboard changes: add metrics: duplicate_fragment_rate, fragment_dedupe_saves_tokens, toolcall_retry_rebill_count. Dashboards to show cost impact by customer so customers can spot anomalies.
maya: can we also update rollout UX: when enabling new runtime that changes fragment_id semantics, console should show "billing impact estimate" and sample delta for an org based on last 7 days. ops needs that before we flip global flag.
frank: ops note: when we add ledger with TTL, memory must be bounded. use memcached sharded store with LRU + TTL, approximate dedupe but fine. Also ensure ledger key includes model + shard to avoid cross-shard misses.
sanjay: tests: create fuzz harness that simulates client retries, truncated reads, and toolcalls producing long outputs. assert billed_tokens == unique_fragments_tokens + final_tool_output_tokens (unless ack-mode).
lisa: I'll own dashboard tiles and product copy. maya please own spec for request_id/session hashing. frank own runtime changes and memcached ledger. sanjay own meter + billing tests.
maya: ack. I'll post a short spec in #eng-platform later.
billing-bot: Alert: created ticket BI-6124 to track "streaming dedupe and truncation billing". Priority: P2.
maya: thanks. let's sync on Tues 11am to review the spec. :thumbsup:
frank: added a note to eng-oncall for any immediate regression after we deploy dedupe.
sanjay: cool. small follow-up: add unit to show when fallback routing (model variant fallback) causes double-billing because two different models run for same request_id — ensure dedupe keys include fallback lineage.
maya: noted — include fallback lineage in spec.
lisa: done. end of thread.
